headline: Gas power plants planned for US data centers could raise the country's power-sector carbon emissions by about 20 percent, a Bloomberg analysis found.
score_reason: Lowered from 6 to 4: the analysis was published on 18 Aug 2026 and the pool item is a late repost with no new development.
importance_line: Climate goals set by Amazon and Microsoft come under pressure and US power-sector emissions could rise, but many of the proposed plants may never be built and the estimate depends on how hard they run.
summary: Bloomberg reports, as carried by Fortune, that 99 proposed data-center gas plants tracked by BloombergNEF, its energy research arm, would emit about 318 million metric tons of carbon dioxide a year at typical running rates, about 20 percent on top of the 1,485 million tons the US power industry emitted last year, and up to a third if run flat out. Not every plant is likely to be built, and Amazon and Microsoft say their climate goals have not changed; Bloomberg published the analysis on 18 Aug 2026.
notes: Old news re-dated by EnergyNow. Read at Fortune's copy of the Bloomberg text; Bloomberg link decoded from Google News, not opened.
